sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the blocks of north-central Millville between East Depot Street at the top and East Vine Street at the bottom, from North Buck Street on the west to North 2nd Street on the east. East Broad Street and East Oak Street cross it, and Penn and North High Streets run north and south through the middle. The west half is mostly dwellings, drawn as small yellow frame houses with their lot lines, with a few stores and a garage with a capacity of twenty cars at the top near Depot Street. The Elk's Home stands on the lower west side near Vine Street, and the North Baptist Church lies in the lower middle between Oak and Vine Streets. The east half is crossed diagonally by a railroad line running from the upper middle to the lower right, with a wood yard, Shaw and Wood, and the Kimball and Prince Lumber Co. yard with its lumber piles and a watchman and fire station beside the tracks. Brick and stone buildings are shown in pink and blue, and water mains are drawn in the streets. Streets are drawn at 66 feet, and only their pipes and block corners mark the edges. Adjoining sheets 8, 15, 17, 3 and 33 are named in the margins. The blank strip along the west edge belongs to sheet 8.
notes: North Buck Street is Buck Street in OpenStreetMap, East Depot, Broad, Oak and Vine are East Depot Street, East Broad Street, East Oak Street and East Vine Street, North High and North 2nd are North High Street and North 2nd Street, Penn is Penn Street.
Buck Street and Penn Street are used as control; Buck Street lies on the west edge of the sheet.
50 ft. East Depot to East Vine, North Buck to North 2nd Streets; Manumuskan track crosses diagonally. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 lies in the middle of downtown Millville, from East Vine Street at the top to East Sassafras Street at the bottom, and from North Buck Street near the west edge to North 2nd Street near the east edge. East Mulberry Street and East Pine Street cross the sheet, and North High Street runs through the centre. The upper part is residential, with the Post Office as a large pink brick building on Mulberry Street. Between Mulberry and Pine Streets lie the Eastern Glass Works, drawn with its sheds and storage buildings west of High Street, and further bottle and glass works east of High Street towards North 2nd Street. South of Pine Street the blocks become commercial: the Levoy Theatre, with movies and vaudeville, a row of stores and other brick buildings line the blocks on both sides of North High Street down to East Sassafras Street. Columbia Avenue enters from the west and runs diagonally across the upper left corner. The lower left corner shows the Maurice River edge with a junk yard and West Pine and West Sassafras Streets leaving the sheet. Brick buildings are pink, frame buildings yellow and sheds blue.
notes: Printed names correspond to modern Buck Street, North High Street, North 2nd Street, East Mulberry Street, East Pine Street and Sassafras Street in OpenStreetMap.
Sheet 2 continues to the north, sheet 4 to the south.
50 ft. Vine to Sassafras, downtown (Post Office, Levoy Theatre, Eastern Glass Works). One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the centre of Millville along Main Street, from East Sassafras Street at the top to the residential blocks south of Smith Street. West Sassafras Street and East Sassafras Street run across the top, and North High Street and North 2nd Street come in from the north to cross East Main Street. South of Main Street they continue as South High Street and South 2nd Street, with Smith Street crossing them below. North Buck Street runs along the west side. The upper part holds the main business district: the L. G. Nester Co. works with a rolling plant in a fireproof building at the upper left, the Mechanics National Bank and the Millville Trust Co. on North High Street, the F.O.E. Club house on Main Street, and rows of brick stores on both sides of Main Street. City Hall stands on the corner of Smith and South High Streets, and Trinity M.E. Church and Trinity Social Hall lie on South 2nd Street. South of Smith Street the blocks thin out into dwellings and open land, with Camp's Lane running down the lower right. The Maurice River runs along the left edge of the sheet. Streets are drawn at 66 feet with water mains marked in them, and the whole sheet is rotated about seven degrees from the page.
notes: Printed names correspond to modern Sassafras Street, Buck Street, North High Street, South High Street, North 2nd Street, South 2nd Street, East Main Street and Smith Street in OpenStreetMap.
Camp's Lane is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
50 ft. Main Street, Sassafras to south of Smith; drawn turned about 7 degrees. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the west side of Millville across the Maurice River from the centre of town, along West Main Street. West Main Street crosses the top of the sheet from the left towards the steel bridge over the river at the upper right, and Corson Drive runs along a park at the top left, with a row of lots fronting it. Below Main Street the blocks are drawn at an angle of about sixteen degrees to the page: Cedar Street, Middle Avenue and Madison Avenue run down the sheet from the upper right to the lower left, crossed by Howard Street and Fulton Street at the left. The lots are long and narrow, most of them holding one dwelling, with a few stores near the Main Street end. Close to the river at the upper right there is a lumber yard with its sheds, a hardware store and other small businesses. A water pipe line runs diagonally down the sheet beside Cedar Street. The lower right part of the sheet is blank, being the low ground beside the river, which curves in a pale blue band along the right edge. Several sheets overlap this one: sheet 4 at the right, sheet 6 at the left, and sheet 26 below.
notes: Printed names correspond to modern West Main Street, Cedar Street, Middle Avenue, Madison Avenue, Howard Street and Fulton Street in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is turned about 16 degrees from north.
50 ft. West Main Street with Cedar, Middle and Madison Avenues, turned about -16 degrees; Maurice River at right. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the residential west side of Millville between North Park Avenue at the left and Cedar Street at the lower right. Maurice Street crosses the upper part, West Main Street runs across the sheet a little below it, and Howard Street and Fulton Street cross the lower part, with Brandriff Avenue running down the middle. The blocks are lined with long narrow lots, nearly all of them with a single frame dwelling drawn in yellow, and there are very few stores or works; the West Side M.E. Church stands at the left edge near Park Avenue, and a small pink and blue cluster of brick buildings lies in the middle between Main and Howard Streets. Corson Drive leaves the sheet at the upper right beside a park, and Cedar Street runs diagonally down the right side, with the lots on either side turned to follow it. The streets are drawn at 66 feet with water mains in them. The sheet is turned about thirteen degrees from north, and the page margin on the right is blank paper which belongs to sheet 5. A compass rose in the upper right corner shows the orientation.
notes: Printed names correspond to modern Maurice Street, West Main Street, North Park Avenue, South Park Avenue, North and South Brandriff Avenue, Howard Street, Fulton Street and Cedar Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Maurice Street drawn here is the northern of two ways of that name in OpenStreetMap; it was left out of the control.
South Park and the church name were read from the overview and are medium confidence.
50 ft. West side, Maurice to Fulton, Park to Cedar, turned about -13 degrees. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 is taken up by the Whitall Tatum Co. Glasstown Works and its bottle works, on the west side of Millville along the Maurice River. The works occupy most of the sheet, drawn as many large buildings: long warehouses and packing sheds in yellow, brick furnace and batch houses in pink, storage buildings, a machine shop, a tool room, a box shop and a clay room, with iron stacks, tanks and a watchman's office. Railroad sidings and spur tracks fan out through the plant from the upper right, where the main lines come together, and a long finished-stock building stands next to the tracks at the upper left. A written table of the works' fire protection, giving the pumps, hose, chemical engines and pressure, is printed in the lower middle. At the right, Columbia Avenue runs diagonally down from the top, West Vine Street crosses the upper right corner, and North Buck Street and Mulberry Street meet near the right edge. West Pine Street leaves the sheet at the bottom. The Maurice River forms a pale blue band along the left side, and the ground beside it is marked as marsh hay. A compass rose in the upper left corner shows the orientation. Only a few streets are drawn, so this sheet has little ordinary street layout.
notes: Printed names correspond to modern West Vine Street, Columbia Avenue, Buck Street, East Mulberry Street and West Pine Street in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is placed from only three points along Buck Street, so it is low confidence and its far left side is placed by the fitted scale and rotation.
50 ft. Whitall Tatum glass works on Buck Street; few streets; helmert along Buck Street. One part.

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 8, in the western part of Millville. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north near the top, and is bounded at the top by West Depot Street, on the left by Dock Street, and on the right by North Buck Street, which runs off the right edge of the sheet. West Broad Street crosses the middle of the sheet and West Oak and West Vine Streets lie below it. Between Dock and Buck Streets the blocks hold frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few small shops along West Depot and West Broad Streets, a row of brick or frame stores on the south side of West Broad Street, and an auto repair and blacksmith and woodworking shop. Dock Street carries a spur track and a 50 foot street width is marked on it; a water pipe of the Millville Water Co. runs along it. Large blocks between West Oak Street and Dock Street are left blank. West of Dock Street the sheet is drawn at an angle: the streets there (Church, Columbia Avenue and West Powell) run diagonally, with houses on narrow lots, a fire department building near the top and a few small works. A compass rose at the top left shows north. A heavy line cuts off the lower left corner, which is drawn turned and forms part 2. Neighbouring sheets 7, 9, 10 and 11 are named at the margins, and a Library map division stamp is printed near the foot.
notes: Street names were read on the overview and on 1:1 crops of West Powell, Church, North, North Buck and West Depot Street only; West Broad, West Oak, West Vine, Dock and Columbia Avenue are medium confidence.
Modern names: West Depot Street, West Broad Street, West Oak Street, West Vine Street, Dock Street, Buck Street (printed North Buck), Church Street, Columbia Avenue and West Powell Street.
John M. Maris Co., manufacturers of druggists' glassware, stands on the diagonal block near North Street.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main grid (Dock, Buck, Depot, Broad, Oak, Vine); 2 lower-left inset turned about -46 degrees (Columbia Avenue, West Broad, West Powell), anchored.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 is the lower left corner of sheet 8, cut off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn turned about 45 degrees from it, with its own north arrow. It shows the west end of Columbia Avenue, which runs across the foot of the part, with West Powell Street running up the left side and West Broad Street leaving it on a diagonal. The block below Columbia Avenue holds a row of frame dwellings with small outbuildings, numbered 570 to 582, and the area between West Powell and West Broad Streets is mostly blank, with a triangular block above Columbia Avenue. A water pipe of the Millville Water Co. is marked in Columbia Avenue and in West Broad Street. The part is a small piece; the sheet number 10 is printed at the left, 9 at the lower left and 8 in the block above Columbia Avenue, showing the neighbouring sheets and the continuation of the map. The part has only one usable junction and is placed from it by an assumed scale and rotation.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Columbia Avenue at West Powell and West Broad Streets) with scale and rotation taken from sheet 10; low confidence.
The modern West Powell node is about 18 m from the West Broad node; the westerly node was used because sheet 10 agreed with it better.
Names read on a crop at about one third reduction and the overview, not 1:1; medium confidence.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main grid (Dock, Buck, Depot, Broad, Oak, Vine); 2 lower-left inset turned about -46 degrees (Columbia Avenue, West Broad, West Powell), anchored.

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 9 shows the industrial district of Millville along the Maurice River and the east side of Columbia Avenue. The sheet is drawn turned about 45 degrees. Most of it is taken up by the works of the Millville Manufacturing Company, which includes the Manantico Bleachery and Dye Works: a large finishing building, bleach houses, wash house, mangle rooms, mercerizing and finishing rooms, a power house, a store house and storage and packing buildings, the Main Cotton Mill and a mill for mule spinning, reeling and twisting with a weaving floor above, and a cotton warehouse of concrete construction near Columbia Avenue. Water power is carried by a head race and a tail race beside the river, and spur tracks and a trestle for coal run through the yards. Each building is described with its construction, sprinkler system, watchman service, fire pumps and hose and water supply; two notes on the south side give this data for the Cotton Mill and the Bleachery. Columbia Avenue runs down the right edge with West Foundry, West McNeal and West Green Streets entering from the right, where the neighbouring sheet 29 is drawn. A flour and grain mill and a store shed stand at the top. A compass rose at the upper left shows north, and the Maurice River crosses the lower left. A lower left piece of the sheet, cut off by a heavy line, is not placed.
notes: Only three hand-picked points, all along Columbia Avenue, place the part (helmert); low confidence, especially for rotation across the sheet.
Columbia Avenue is drawn slightly curved on the sheet.
The lower left piece of the sheet (West Sharp Street and the Millville Electric Light and Water Co.) has no street junction and is not placed.
50 ft. Millville Mfg Co works, turned about 45 degrees. Part 1 placed along Columbia Avenue (helmert); part 2 (lower left, West Sharp, Electric Light and Water Co, Head Race) unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower left: West Sharp Street, Millville Electric Light and Water Co, Head Race (no street junction; needs step 6b carried points from sheet 29-1 or 12-1).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows a residential district of western Millville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 45 degrees, so that Church Street and Columbia Avenue run across the page and West McNeal, West Green and West Powell Streets run up and down. Archer Street crosses near the top, with North Street and Church Street below it, and Columbia Avenue runs across the foot of the sheet. The blocks hold frame dwellings, mostly of two storeys, on regular lots, with some outbuildings; a row of dwellings stands at the top left. The R. D. Wood Public School, a brick building with a long front, stands in the middle of the right side. A few small shops and a garage are drawn at the foot, and a small block of buildings lies along West Depot Street near the right edge. Dock Street and a diagonal street run from the upper middle to the right edge, and a compass rose at the right shows the turned north. Block numbers 78 to 91 are printed with alternate numbers in brackets, and neighbouring sheets 8, 9, 11, 12 and 29 are named at the margins. A scale of feet is printed at the lower right. A water pipe is shown in the main streets, with fire hydrants.
notes: Names read on the overview and on 1:1 crops of building number labels only; street names are medium confidence.
Modern names: Archer Street, North Street, Church Street, Columbia Avenue, West McNeal Street, West Green Street, West Powell Street, Dock Street, West Depot Street and West Broad Street.
R. D. Wood Public School stands at the right of the sheet.
50 ft. Turned about -46 degrees; Archer, North, Church, Columbia, McNeal to Broad. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers a residential and commercial part of western Millville around the crossing of Dock and Buck Streets, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north near the top. West and East McNeal Street run across near the top, West and East Green Street and West and East Powell Street below them, and West and East Depot Street across the foot. Dock Street runs down the left side, with a spur track in it, North Buck Street down the middle and North High Street along the right edge. The blocks are lined with frame dwellings, mostly two storeys, with sheds and garages in the rear, and the streets are drawn at 50 or 60 feet. St. Mary Magdalen Roman Catholic Church with a parochial school and a convent stands on the block between West Powell and West Depot Streets east of Dock Street. A few small stores and a rectory are shown, and the upper left is cut by diagonal streets: Archer, North and West Green, which belong to the grid of sheet 10 and run off at an angle. A compass rose at the left shows north, and a scale of feet is printed at the foot. Block numbers 60 to 79 are printed with alternate numbers in brackets, and neighbouring sheets 2, 8, 10, 13 and 33 are named at the margins.
notes: Street names read on the overview and on 1:1 crops of the Dock Street area; medium confidence.
Modern names: Buck Street (printed North Buck) and Archer Street; the diagonal West Green on the left follows the old street lines of sheet 10.
50 ft. Grid McNeal to Depot, Dock to High. One part.

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 12 shows a residential district at the north end of western Millville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 45 degrees. Church Street runs up the left edge, North Street and Archer Street lie further right, and West Sharp Street crosses the top diagonally from the left to the upper right. McChesney Street, West Foundry Street and West McNeal Street cross the sheet from side to side below it. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings of one and two storeys on regular lots, with outbuildings. The Millville Manufacturing Company's warehouse stands on the diagonal block at the left, the Second M. E. Church stands at the lower left, an apartment building stands at the lower right and a few small shops are drawn in the middle. A rectangle at the upper right is cut off by a heavy line and forms part 2, an inset at the same orientation with Sharp Street drawn again. The compass rose is printed near the inset. Neighbouring sheets 10, 13, 29 and 30 are named at the margins; the numbers 81 to 84, 101 and 206 appear in the blocks as block numbers.
notes: Names read on the overview and partial 1:1 crops only; medium confidence.
Modern names: Sharp Street, Mc Chesney Street, North Street, Archer Street, West Foundry Street, West McNeal Street and Church Street.
Millville Mfg. Co. warehouse and Second M. E. Church are drawn at the left of the sheet.
50 ft. Turned about +44 degrees. Two parts: 1 main (West Sharp, McChesney, Archer, Foundry, McNeal, Church); 2 inset upper right (West Sharp, Archer), anchored.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 is a rectangular inset at the upper right, set off by a heavy line, that carries West Sharp Street beyond the top edge of the main part. Sharp Street runs diagonally across the inset, rising to the right, and Archer Street enters it from below as a vertical street with water pipes of the Peoples Water Co. and the Millville Water Co. The inset is drawn at 50 feet to an inch at the same turn as the main part, about 45 degrees. A row of frame dwellings and sheds on the north side of Sharp Street, in the block numbered 206 (497), is shown in detail, with house numbers 190 to 202 along the front. The south side is blank; the lettering 'No Exposure' is printed along the right and left edges, meaning that no building adjoins that side. sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the northern edge of the built-up area of western Millville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north near the top. West and East Foundry Street cross the middle of the sheet and West and East McNeal Street the foot, with Dock Street down the left side, North Buck Street near the middle and North High Street at the right edge. The built blocks lie in the lower third: frame dwellings of one and two storeys on regular lots, with outbuildings, the Millville Laundry, a shop building in blue, and a small group of buildings at the right with a store at the corner of North High Street. The upper two thirds is mostly blank open ground crossed by a railroad curving from the left to the top and then running off to the right edge, drawn in light double lines. A diagonal line marks a boundary at the left. A compass rose and the north arrow are printed at the upper left and a scale of feet at the foot. sheet-14-1.description: Sheet 14 part 1 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, and shows the industrial ground east of North High Street in the north of Millville. The left third is a column of large vacant blocks numbered 112 to 114, laid out between East Harrison at the head of the sheet, East Elmer and East McChesney (both marked as not opened) and East Foundry at the foot, with North High Street along the left edge and North 2nd Street running down the middle between the blocks. A ball park occupies the block at upper centre, and a Standard Oil Co. depot with oil tanks stands beside the railroad at North 2nd Street, with a coal yard in the lower left block. A broad double-track railroad, the West Jersey and Seashore line of the Pennsylvania Railroad, crosses the sheet diagonally from the foot of the sheet to the upper right with water mains marked beside it, and a spur curves off to the left to cross North High Street and runs past the coal yard. The right and lower half of the sheet is the T. C. Wheaton and Co. bottle manufacturing works, with its furnaces, lehrs, batch houses, packing rooms, warehouses, machine shops, an art department, a paper box factory and a grinding mill, bounded on the east by North 3rd Street, which runs obliquely. G Street is lettered across the foot. A boxed area at upper right, divided by a heavy line, is a separate part of the sheet. Sheets 13, 30 and 33 are named at the edges.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows a residential and light-commercial district of north-central Millville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about four and a half degrees from true north. Three east-west streets cross it: D Street near the top, East Broad Street through the middle and East Oak Street along the lower part, with North 2nd, North 3rd and North 4th Streets running north and south. Wheaton Avenue cuts diagonally across the block north of East Broad Street between North 3rd and North 4th Streets. Most lots carry frame dwellings with small outbuildings. The larger buildings include a private truck garage and a brick-faced warehouse used for groceries north of East Broad Street, the First M.P. Church and a building-materials store on North 2nd Street, a bakery and a small group of shops beside Wheaton Avenue, a Jewish club house on East Oak Street and a coal yard in the block between North 3rd and North 4th Streets. Water pipes of the Millville Water Co. and the Peoples Water Co. are marked in the streets, with hydrants. Blocks are numbered 33, 34, 35, 42 and 43 with older numbers in brackets. A compass rose and scale of feet are printed on the sheet, and the neighbouring sheets 16, 17, 20 and 33 are named at the edges.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 lies in north-central Millville and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. East Broad Street crosses the sheet in the upper middle and East Oak Street runs along the bottom, with State Street lettered between them in the central blocks and D Street at the top. North 5th, North 6th and North 7th Streets run north and south. The upper half is dominated by the grounds of Millville Memorial High School, a large fire-proof building built in 1924 with an auditorium and gymnasium, standing in an otherwise blank block above East Broad Street; the northern streets are marked as not open. Below East Broad Street the blocks hold frame dwellings with small outbuildings and an apartment building and a contractors' supplies yard on State Street. A bottling works and ice-cream plant with concrete and tile construction stands in the block between North 6th and North 7th Streets, reached by a narrow lane that widens at the works. A compass rose and scale of feet are printed on the sheet, and the neighbouring sheets 15, 18, 20, 33 and 34 are named at the edges. Water pipes of the Millville Water Co. and the Peoples Water Co. run in the streets.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers a residential district in the east of Millville at 50 feet to an inch, between East Oak Street at the top and East Pine Street at the bottom, with East Vine and Mulberry Streets between. North 2nd, North 3rd and North 4th Streets run north and south. A railroad line of the West Jersey and Seashore system crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, cutting through the blocks and across North 3rd Street. Most lots carry frame dwellings and sheds. The larger buildings include a garage and furniture storage building (Thomas O. Troth) on East Oak Street, a coal yard beside the railroad, a filling station on a triangular lot at the left edge, St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church on North 3rd Street, the First M.E. Church at the lower left corner, an ice plant with a tinner and glass-painting shops beside the track, and the Northeastern Public School at the upper right. Water pipes of both Millville water companies are marked in the streets. A compass rose and scale of feet are printed on the left. The adjoining sheets 15, 18, 19 and 2 are named at the margins.
notes: Modern names: East Oak Street, East Vine Street, East Mulberry Street, East Pine Street.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers six residential blocks in the east of Millville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page. The area is bounded by East Oak Street at the top and East Pine Street at the bottom, with Vine and Mulberry Streets crossing between them, and by North 5th Street on the left and North 7th Street along the right edge; a strip of the blocks west of North 5th Street, towards North 4th, is drawn at the left margin. Nearly every lot carries a frame dwelling, most of one or two storeys, with small rear sheds, stables, hen houses and garages. Commercial and industrial use is slight: a blacksmith and wheelwright shop stands on the block west of North 5th Street between Vine and Mulberry, a concrete-block auto storage building and a concrete-block garage stand on the blocks to the north, a small power building of a garment manufacturer stands on the block between North 6th and North 7th Streets south of Vine, and a brick dwelling and a sign painting shop appear elsewhere. The sheet gives water pipes of the Millville Water Co. and the Peoples Water Co. (P.W. Co.) in every street, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes, and the street widths (66 feet) at the block corners. The blocks are numbered 15 to 24 with alternate numbers in brackets. A compass rose and a scale of feet are printed in the block east of North 6th Street. Neighbouring sheets 16, 17, 20, 34 and 35 are named at the edges.
notes: The modern names are East Oak Street, East Vine Street, East Mulberry Street and East Pine Street.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows the centre of Millville at 50 feet to an inch, from East Pine Street at the top down through East Sassafras and East Main Streets to Smith Street, and from North and South 2nd Street at the left to North and South 4th Street at the right. The upper left holds the First Presbyterian Church with its parsonage, the Millville Public School, Culver Public School, a fire department building and a library. East Main Street carries First Baptist Church, Christ Episcopal Church, a Vineland pants company garage and a row of frame dwellings. Below East Main Street are dwellings, an ice cream factory, a dress manufacturing plant lettered Ayres and Doughty, and in the lower left corner streets that run on a slanting grid. North of East Sassafras Street a lumber yard with sheds (J. S. Hoffman) and a machine shop stand beside a service lane. At the upper right the railroad of the West Jersey and Seashore line passes a garage and auto painting shop. A compass rose and scale of feet are printed on the sheet, and sheets 17, 20, 21 and 22 are named at the edges.
notes: Modern names: East Pine Street, Sassafras Street, East Main Street, Smith Street.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers part of east-central Millville at 50 feet to an inch, from East Pine Street at the top through East Sassafras Street and East Main Street to Smith Street, with North 5th, North 6th and North 7th Streets and, below East Main Street, South 5th, South 6th and South 7th Streets. The tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad cross the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, forming triangular blocks and splitting into a yard at the lower right where the sheet joins sheet 31. Nearly all lots in the blocks carry frame dwellings with small sheds. Other buildings include a larger frame building at the corner of East Sassafras Street and North 6th Street, an auto repair shop on East Main Street, the A.M.E. Church on South 5th Street and a block of unbuilt lots in the lower middle. Water pipes of the Millville and Peoples water companies are lettered in the streets. A compass rose and the scale of feet are printed at the lower right. Sheets 18, 19, 22, 31 and 35 are named at the margins.
notes: Modern names: East Pine Street, Sassafras Street, East Main Street, Smith Street.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers a residential district in the south-east of Millville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the street grid runs about 22 degrees from the page edges, with a compass rose at the upper left. Florence Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, and Garrison Avenue, a wider street that runs obliquely, cuts the upper right corner. South 2nd, South 3rd and South 4th Streets run down the sheet, the 2nd Street side being the left margin, and Railroad Street, also lettered Whitall Street, runs along the foot beside the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore and Pennsylvania railroads, which are drawn across the bottom. Almost every lot carries a frame dwelling of one or two storeys with outbuildings, in long narrow plots with house numbers (the 200s and 300s) printed along each frontage. Two blocks west of South 3rd Street near the top hold a show room, an electric apparatus works and a small bakehouse with an oven. Near the foot a candy manufacturer, Wm. Wood, occupies a brick building shown in blue on the Railroad Street frontage. The left third of the sheet, west of South 2nd Street, is mostly blank with a few scattered dwellings and part of block 4, and the lower left corner is occupied by a scale of feet and a stamp of the map division. Water pipes of the two water companies run in the middle of the streets. Neighbouring sheets 19, 22, 23 and 24 are named at the edges.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 lies in the south-east of Millville, east of sheet 21, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 25 degrees from the page edges. Florence Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right, and South 4th, South 5th and South 6th Streets run down it, with South 4th Street at the left margin and South 6th Street near the right. Garrison Avenue, a wide street that runs obliquely, crosses the upper part of the sheet from the upper left to the right. Railroad Street, also lettered Whitall Street, runs along the foot of the built-up area beside the railroad tracks, which run across the lower part of the sheet and curve to the north-east at the right. The blocks between Garrison and Florence and between Florence and Railroad Street are filled with frame dwellings of one or two storeys on narrow lots, with sheds, garages and hen houses behind them and the house numbers printed along each front. Narrow alleys divide the blocks, and the water pipes of two companies are drawn in the streets. The block at the right, beyond South 6th Street, holds the works of the Millville Iron Works Inc., a steel machine shop with concrete piers, brick and concrete walls and a trussed roof, with its office, shown without a watchman or heat and lighted by electricity. A coal and wood yard (the name begins Corson) stands in the block west of South 5th Street near the foot. The lower right quarter is blank, held for the railroad curve and for another sheet, and carries a stamp of the map division and a scale of feet.

sheet-23-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 23 is the main map of the South Millville Works of the Whitall Tatum Co., a flint glass factory, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The works occupy nearly the whole part, east of the blocks of sheets 21 and 24 and bounded on the right by South 2nd Street, which runs down the right edge. Almost nothing else is drawn: there are no house lots. The buildings are shown in pink for brick or fireproof construction and yellow for frame, with their uses lettered inside them: batch house, sand room, mould shop, machine shops, tank furnaces, annealing lehrs, a pot room, a gas producer house, stock and packing rooms, experimental machine and furnace buildings and offices, a locomotive house, a sample room, a paper ware house and a large bottle storage building. Railroad sidings and tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad (the West Jersey and Seashore) enter from the upper right where they cross South 2nd Street, and run through the works between the buildings; a coal pile with a concrete trestle stands in the lower middle. Water pipes, fire hydrants, hose connections and detailed notes on watchman, power, heat and lights are printed throughout. The upper left and lower left corners of the sheet are cut off by heavy lines marked No Exposure and hold separate insets (parts 2 and 3). A scale of feet and the Sanborn copyright note stand in the lower left of the main part, and the sheet number and date stamp in the upper right.

sheet-24-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 24 is the main map of the southern edge of Millville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It is cut from the rest of the sheet by a heavy dividing line that runs from the top edge diagonally down to a corner at the right and then across to the right edge, so the part covers the left side of the sheet and its whole lower half. South 2nd Street, a long street leaning down to the right, crosses the part from the top (where it meets Maylin Street) to the foot, with South 3rd Street beside it on the right. Garfield, Noble, Cherry and Plum Streets run across it, and Hoover Avenue and Walnut Lane join them on the lower left. Myrtle Street appears at the far left. Most of the lots hold small frame dwellings in long narrow plots, many with house numbers printed at the fronts, with a church, the South Millville School and an auto repair shop among the few other uses. Petticoat Branch crosses the upper middle as a small stream, and marsh land is lettered towards the lower left. Parts of the sheet to the left and top are blank, and the lower left holds a scale of feet and the copyright note. A compass rose stands at the left edge.

sheet-24-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 24 is the box at the upper right of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy line that runs diagonally from the top edge to a corner and then across to the right edge. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, turned about ten degrees from the page, and shows a district of open, thinly built streets in the south of Millville. Whitall Avenue crosses the top from the lower left to the upper right, and South 2nd and South 3rd Streets run down from it, with Valatia Avenue and Henderson Avenue crossing them lower down, Peek Avenue, a narrow street, at the bottom left and Mickle Street at the right edge. Plum Street is lettered along the top left. The blocks are numbered 24, 25, 248, 249, 253 and 960, with alternate numbers in brackets. Most lots are large, with scattered frame dwellings and sheds and some poultry houses, a garage for 75 cars on Whitall Avenue beside South 3rd Street, and a few small dwellings along South 2nd Street. Most of the lower half of the box is blank, held for the sheet to the south. Water pipes of the Millville Water Co. and the Peoples Water Co. are drawn in the streets, and street widths of 33, 50 and 60 feet are given at the corners.

sheet-25-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 25 is the upper and largest part of the page, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left (about 66 degrees). It shows a thinly built district in the south of Millville along South 2nd Street, which runs across the page, with South 3rd Street and South 4th Street above it. Henderson Avenue, Stratton Avenue, Menantico Avenue and Beaupel Avenue run up the page from South 2nd Street; Beaupel Avenue is marked not open, and Peek Avenue and a street lettered Drive leave South 2nd Street at the lower left. Arbutus Avenue crosses the right side of the part diagonally. The large blocks between the avenues (numbered 215, 216, 216A, 216B and 251) are mostly empty, with a few dwellings and sheds near the corners. Along both sides of South 2nd Street stands a row of small one- and two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, numbered 1010 to 1130, with hen houses and stables behind them in block 217. Water pipes of the Millville Water Co. are drawn in South 2nd and South 3rd Streets and in Stratton and Menantico Avenues, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. A heavy line along the bottom separates this part from the two West Main Street strips drawn below it on the same page. Sheet 24 adjoins at the left edge.

The street runs straight across the page with deep, narrow lots on both sides, numbered 1501 to 1540. sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the south-western edge of Millville's built-up area, east and south of the blocks of sheet 27, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with a compass rose at the right. Fulton Street runs across the top left and Race Street below it, both rising to the right, crossed by South Park Avenue, Penn Avenue on the left and Cedar Street, which runs diagonally from the upper middle down to the lower left. Madison Avenue and Middle Avenue lead off Cedar Street to the south-east and Race Street continues as a diagonal road across the right half. Maple Street and Ireland Avenue cross at the lower left. Washington Avenue and Hamilton Avenue are laid out as long, nearly empty avenues running south-west and south through the middle. Houses stand mainly in the upper left, around Cedar Street and Madison Avenue, with frame dwellings on narrow lots, and a foundry, John B. Madden iron foundry, near Cedar and Madison; poultry houses stand beside Maple Street. The lower and right parts are open land: a swamp and the Whitemarsh Run to the east, Silver Lake in the lower right and another stream crossing the lower left. sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 shows the western part of Millville along West Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. West Main Street crosses the upper middle of the sheet from left to right, with Maurice Street above it and Howard Street, Fulton, Race, Maple Street and Ireland below it, so that the sheet reads as a series of nearly horizontal streets. They are crossed by Mulford Avenue and Pike Avenue near the top, by North Park Avenue and South Park Avenue at the right edge, by Brown Street leaning to the left, and by Arlington Avenue, Cemetery Avenue and Penn Avenue lower down. Houses of one or two storeys stand in rows along West Main Street, Howard Street and Maurice Street, with the Western School at the right on South Park Avenue; the blocks south of Fulton Street are mostly empty, laid out in lots with a few dwellings. Large blocks lie at the left and are crossed by Brown Street, which runs obliquely. The Maurice River runs across the upper left corner, a small stream at the lower left, and Mt. Pleasant Cemetery is lettered at the left margin. Blocks are numbered 403 to 407, 424 to 438 and 493, with alternate numbers in brackets. sheet-28-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 28 is the main part of the page, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 15 degrees to the left. It covers the west side of Millville on both sides of West Main Street from South Beech Street at the left to Chestnut Street and Mount Pleasant Cemetery at the right. North of West Main Street, North Spruce, North Pearl, North Laurel and North Sharp Streets run diagonally up the page to Cooper Street and Lake Street, laid out in long narrow lots with scattered dwellings; Cooper Road (Flask Road) and New Beaver Dam Road (Carmel Road) leave the area to the west, and the corner of Union Lake shows at the upper left. South of West Main Street the blocks between South Beech, South Spruce, South Pearl, South Laurel and Chestnut Streets reach Cherry Street and Fairton Road, with a vacant tract beyond. The buildings are mostly frame dwellings with hen houses and sheds; a church stands on North Pearl Street. Water pipes of the Millville Water Co. and the Peoples Water Co. run in the main streets. The parenthesised names record older names: South Spruce Street was Cedar, South Pearl Street was South Spruce, South Laurel Street was Walnut and North Sharp Street was Park.
notes: North Sharp (Park) is today Sharp Street; New Beaver Dam Road is Carmel Road.
Lake Street is not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-28-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 28 is the strip across the top of the page, separated from the main part by a heavy line, and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 13 degrees to the left. It shows West Main Street west of South Beech Street, on the western edge of Millville, continuing to the left onto the bottom strip of sheet 25. West Main Street runs across the top of the strip with deep lots on both sides; to the south, Fairton Road leaves South Beech Street at the right, opposite Cherry Street, and runs off to the left, and New Beaver Dam Road (Carmel Road) leaves the corner at the upper right. The lots hold scattered frame dwellings, hen houses and a chicken breeding house, with large vacant tracts marked vacant beyond. A 6 inch water pipe of the Millville Water Co. runs in West Main Street. A corner of Union Lake shows at the left edge, below the heavy line, where it belongs to the main part.
notes: Placed from Beech Street / West Main Street (detected), Beech Street / Cherry Street / Fairton Road (hand-picked) and a point on the modern West Main Street centreline at the strip's west end, at the atlas scale; low confidence at the west end.

sheet-29-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 29 covers the east shore of Union Lake on the northwest side of Millville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (about 44 degrees). Most of the part is the open water of Union Lake, with a row of summer cottages along the curving shore at the top and right, and the Parkside Rest cottages at the head of a cove; a road curves round behind them. To the lower right lie the streets near the dam and the Millville Manufacturing Co.: Columbia Avenue runs down the page past Biggs Street and West Sharp Street, with Hogan Street and Canal Street to the east, an alley behind West Sharp Street and an athletic field. Cotton ware houses of the Millville Mfg. Co. stand by the lake shore above Biggs Street, and its wooden box shop and ware house stand beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks in the lower right corner, with the Millville Water Co. standpipe. Below the railroad, West Foundry and West McNeal Streets run between Columbia Avenue and Church Street, lined with frame dwellings. A heavy line across the lower left separates this part from the Union Lake Park part of the page.
notes: Hogan Street and Biggs Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
Control lies in the lower right corner (six junctions on Columbia Avenue and Church Street); the lake shore at the top is extrapolated.

sheet-30-1.description: Sheet 30 part 1 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covering the gas works and electric light plant at the northeast edge of the built-up part of Millville. North 2nd Street runs up the page near the left, with East Elizabeth (not opened) crossing at the top, East Cypress at mid-sheet and East Harrison near the foot, all running east from it. North High Street is lettered along the left edge. The largest feature is the Cumberland County Gas Co. works, which fills block 118 and part of block 119: three gas holders, one of 1,500,000 cubic feet drawn as a circle, a retort house, purifier house, meter house, pump house, engine room, a coal shed beside the railroad, a carpenter shop and an office. The Millville Electric Light Co. stands to the south with its engine and dynamo house, a coal pile and a cooling tank. A few small dwellings with numbered lots lie along North 2nd Street at the southern end, and a ball park occupies the lower block near the foot of the sheet. A railroad with several tracks, marked P.R.R. on the sheet, runs diagonally through the right side from lower centre to the upper right corner, with a siding curving off to the lower right, and water pipes are marked beside it. The area at upper left is cut out as a separate inset. Sheet 14 adjoins at the bottom and right.
notes: East Elizabeth, East Cypress and the east end of East Harrison are lettered Not Opened east of North 2nd Street.
Anchored on East Harrison and North 2nd Street at the atlas scale; low confidence.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (gas works, Harrison / North 2nd), anchored; 2 box upper left (Millville Hospital, North Buck, drawn displaced from its true place), anchored.

sheet-30-2.description: Sheet 30 part 2 is a boxed area at the upper left of the sheet, divided from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It shows the blocks west of North High Street and is set into the sheet out of its true position, so that the North High Street along its right edge lies where North 2nd Street runs on the main map. North Buck Street forms the left edge, with the sheet number and the notation No Exposure marked outside it. Between them lie two blocks: the upper, block 104, holds Millville Hospital with its contagious disease wards, laundry and a nurses home, with the hospital building shown in tile and drawn with vapor heat and gas chemical extinguishers; the lower, block 103, holds scattered frame dwellings on small lots with sheds and a few concrete block outbuildings. East Cypress, marked Not Opened, bounds the hospital block above, and East Harrison separates it from the dwellings below. West Harrison Street is lettered at the left edge. A fire alarm box stands at the corner of North High Street, and water pipes of the Millville Water Co. run in the streets. The adjoining sheet 14 is named at the right of the lower block. Because the scale, rotation and position of the box differ from those of the main map, it is treated as its own part.
notes: The box is drawn displaced from its true position, with North High Street on the box's right edge; it is placed from East Harrison and North High Street alone.
The distance from North Buck Street to North High Street is drawn about 6 percent shorter than the modern streets, so Buck Street was left out of the fit.
Low confidence: one measured point plus a derived point.

sheet-32-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 32 is the main part of the page, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 23 degrees to the left. It covers the northern edge of Millville along Wheaton Avenue, which runs up the page from Coombs Road at the bottom towards Whitaker Avenue at the top. West of Wheaton Avenue, Caloris Avenue runs to the left past small lots, with Edgewood Avenue and White Street at the lower left and East Albertson Avenue crossing the lower left diagonally. East of Wheaton Avenue, Overbrook Avenue curves round from Wheaton Avenue to Coombs Road, with Kemble Avenue between them, laid out in narrow lots of a recent development. The district is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings, stores and sheds along Wheaton Avenue and in the new lots, and large vacant blocks numbered 99C, 220, 221, 222 and 224. Whitaker Avenue crosses the upper right corner. A water pipe of the Millville Water Co. runs in Wheaton Avenue. The inset in the upper left corner is part 2.
notes: Edgewood Avenue and White Street are not in OpenStreetMap; East Albertson Avenue is today Albertson Street.
The junction of Wheaton and Whitaker Avenues lies just beyond the top of this part; it is drawn on the inset (part 2).

sheet-32-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 32 is the inset in the upper left corner of the page, drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the same rotation as the main part. It continues Wheaton Avenue north of Whitaker Avenue to the city line between Millville and Landis Township, which is drawn as a dash-dot line across the top of the inset, marked city limits. Wheaton Avenue runs up the middle of the inset with Whitaker Avenue leaving it to the right at the bottom. East of Wheaton Avenue stand the concrete-block buildings of Friedrich & Dimmock (no watchman; heat hot water; power and lights electric), hen houses and dwellings; west of it are dwellings, a green house and an oyster shell grinding works. A water pipe of the Millville Water Co. runs in Wheaton Avenue.
notes: Placed from the one junction, Wheaton Avenue / Whitaker Avenue, at the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.
Landis Township is today the City of Vineland.
100 ft. Two parts: 1 (main) Wheaton Avenue from Coombs Road to Whitaker Avenue; 2 (inset, upper left) Wheaton Avenue north of Whitaker Avenue at the Landis Township line.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the blocks of north-central Millville between East Broad Street at the foot of the sheet and the cross streets D to I above it, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. North 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets run up the page, the grid being turned a few degrees from the sheet edge, and Wheaton Avenue cuts across it diagonally from the middle of the sheet to the upper right, with Central Street crossing near the top. Most of the area is frame dwellings on narrow lots, with house numbers marked, alternating with larger numbered blocks. Distinctive buildings include a garage with pilastered concrete walls on Wheaton Avenue at F Street, a coal yard and a Pilgrim Holiness church near North 2nd and E Street, the Millville Foundry Co. and a machine shop near Central Street, a standpipe and ground of the Peoples Water Co. at the top, and the Dixie Ice Co. and Crew Levick Co. oil depot beside the railroad at left. A broad band of tracks of the railroad, with its yards, platform sheds, a water tank, a passenger depot and a freight house, runs up the left side from East Broad Street, west of North 2nd Street, with North High Street and several short cross streets (East Foundry, McNeal, Green, Powell, Depot) drawn at the left edge. Water pipes of the two water companies run in the streets. The adjoining sheets 2, 13, 14, 15 and 16 are named at the edges. The lower blocks east of North 5th Street and the area below D Street are drawn but partly blank, and a Princeton library stamp falls in the lower margin.
notes: East McNeal, East Foundry and the other cross streets at the left edge are drawn only in part; the junctions with North High Street lie off the sheet.
100 ft. Letter streets D to I, North 2nd to 5th, Wheaton Avenue, West Jersey and Seashore yards. One part.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers the northeast edge of Millville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. A grid of streets runs from E Street and D Street at the top through East Broad Street, East Oak Street and East Vine Street to Mulberry Street at the bottom, crossed by North 7th to North 12th Streets; North 10th, 11th and 12th Streets are marked as not opened in the lower right. Only the western blocks are built up, with scattered frame dwellings and poultry houses, and a few lots hold a cork company works and an auto painting shop. Most blocks are numbered lots with no buildings. At the right the diagonal Mays Landing Road and Hance's Bridge lead to a bridge over the Maurice River tributary shown as a stream at the top right, and the large unplatted area at the lower right is Brinton Park. A compass rose and scale of 100 feet to one inch are printed on the sheet, and the sheet marks no exposure along its east edge. Neighbouring sheets 16, 18, 33, 35 and 36 are named at the margins.
notes: Modern names: East Broad Street, East Oak Street, East Vine Street, East Mulberry Street; Hance's Bridge appears as Hance Bridge Road.
Names were read at overview scale and on a few 1:1 crops; the street list may omit or misrender small lettering (low to medium confidence).

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 covers the eastern edge of Millville at 100 feet to an inch. Mulberry Street runs along the top, then East Pine, East Sassafras and East Main Streets, Woodland Avenue and Oakland Avenue in turn down the sheet. North 7th to North 12th Streets cross the upper half and South 8th to South 12th Streets the lower. The blocks along East Main Street and between East Pine and East Sassafras Streets are built up with frame dwellings, while those at the top, right and bottom are numbered lots without buildings. A large vacant lot at the left lies beside the railroad corridor of the West Jersey and Seashore line, lettered Railroad Boulevard, not opened, in the lower left, and a yellow-coloured building stands on a lot beside it. A stream, Whitemarsh Run, is lettered near the bottom right. A compass rose and the scale of 100 feet to one inch are printed on the sheet. Sheets 18, 20, 31, 34 and 36 are named at the margins.
notes: Modern names: East Mulberry Street, East Pine Street, Sassafras Street, East Main Street.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 is the eastern edge of the platted town of Millville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Streets laid out on paper run from Mulberry Street at the top through East Pine Street, East Sassafras Street, East Main Street, Woodland Avenue and Oakland Avenue, crossed by North 12th, 13th and 14th Streets and South 12th to 17th Streets. Many are lettered as not opened, and almost all of the blocks are numbered, empty lots; the few buildings stand along North 13th Street and East Sassafras Street, at a saw mill with a gas engine in the upper left and on lots on East Main Street. Hankin's Pond and the stream feeding it occupy the upper right, with Ruland Street on its western bank. Two roads, Leaming's Mill Road and Cumberland Road, run diagonally to the lower right. A small stream, Whitemarsh Run, crosses the lower left. A compass rose and scale of 100 feet to one inch are printed on the sheet, and sheets 34 and 35 are named at the margins.
notes: Modern names: East Mulberry Street, East Pine Street, Sassafras Street, East Main Street.
